summary: The stance is clear (ordinary Git, no adoption protocol), but it is not implementable as written: the ADR never says whether Kyyn itself pushes or what the separate 'remote publication' report is.

questions.text: Does Kyyn itself push (or fetch) after local acceptance, automatically or via a separate command, or is publication entirely the user's own Git step?
questions.reason: Decides whether accept gets transport, remote and credential handling; the ADR says the user/agent pushes yet also asks Kyyn to 'report local acceptance and remote publication separately'.

questions.text: What states and target remote/branch does the remote-publication report have, and is it stored, returned once, or derived from refs?
questions.reason: Decides whether anything is persisted per acceptance; the ADR only rules out an 'adoption state machine' and defines no fields or target.

questions.text: What makes a root 'unknown' (marker, validation cache, or always revalidate), and what happens when its validation fails?
questions.reason: Changes the loader, any stored marker/cache and failure behaviour of every validated operation; the ADR says only that unknown roots are validated on load.

questions.text: Is rebasing an unaccepted evolution one atomic Kyyn operation or a manual sequence, and what happens to partial failures and the old results/diff?
questions.reason: Atomicity of a half-rebased evolution (new revision, old schema) is open; the ADR lists the steps and says old attempts need not be retained.

questions.text: How are the explicit repository and KB path supplied and validated, and which operations count as 'semantic'?
questions.reason: Per-call argument vs session/config binding changes every tool signature and error case; the ADR only requires explicit paths and no ambient cwd.

questions.text: May a user-made merge commit that fails validation serve as the base for the next local acceptance?
questions.reason: Decides whether accept's precondition includes a valid base; the ADR says the user 'checks the resulting KB' and Kyyn validates unknown roots, which pull in different directions.

questions.text: Does Kyyn show a derived 'behind local head' indicator for unaccepted evolutions, or is staleness only discovered when accept's CAS fails?
questions.reason: User-visible status on listing/validation; the ADR forbids a permanent Stale lifecycle but says nothing about a computed indicator.

questions.text: May conflict resolution rebase commits already accepted locally, or must it merge so accepted commit ids stay stable?
questions.reason: Decides what accepted workspace records can safely reference; the ADR allows 'merge/rebase' and says accepted workspaces remain historical records.

questions.text: Do outbound plugin side effects fire at local acceptance or only after publication, and what happens to them if the push is rejected and the acceptance is rewritten?
questions.reason: Effects without matching published history may need compensation or a pending queue; the ADR says only that Git transport gains no authority to call plugins.

questions.text: When validating a root that arrived through Git, may checks call outbound plugins, or only pure local checks?
questions.reason: Sets the validator's trust boundary and whether a transport-originated mode is needed; closest text is 'Git transport does not gain authority to call outbound plugins'.
